title: COMP-3 packed decimal — two digits per byte, sign nibble in the last half-byte
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PACKED-AMOUNT.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3 stores 9 digits + sign in CEILING(9/2) =
      *> 5 bytes. Each digit nibble is 0x0..0x9; the LAST nibble is
      *> the sign (0xC = positive, 0xD = negative, 0xF = unsigned).
      *> Reading the same bytes as DISPLAY produces garbage. The
      *> Java port to BigDecimal must understand this layout when
      *> migrating data files in place.
       01  WS-AMT    PIC S9(7)V99 USAGE COMP-3.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           MOVE +1234567.89 TO WS-AMT.
           STOP RUN.
notes: COMP-3 is the workhorse mainframe numeric storage. Migrating to a Java BigDecimal loses the byte-exact layout — fine if all consumers also migrate, fatal if any legacy reader still parses the file. Surface the packed-decimal layout AND the consumer enumeration.
